findings: The frozen 60-day daily workload is substantially harder than the short P2A/P2B workloads.

S4 remains numerically qualified on all four tested materials. B11 and B16 are DAILY_APPROXIMATE; B02 and B05 show candidate-specific daily storage-extremum timing errors of 16 and 19 days against a zero-day R64-vs-R128 comparator.
G8 is numerically qualified for B11 and B16 and has zero daily flux-sign mismatch, zero reversal-sequence mismatch and zero reversal-timing error in those cases.

G8 is NUMERICAL_BLOCKED for B02 and B05 under the frozen candidate dt=0.01 day, with iterative Heun corrector non-convergence. This is a practical robustness failure under the frozen P3 numerical policy.

For qualified 60-day cases, the current Python Layer-ROM implementation is slower than the compiled R128 Reference harness: S4 ratios are about 2.0-2.7 and G8 about 3.0-3.3. Earlier short-horizon speed signals therefore do not transfer to this implementation/workload.
correction_note: The persisted successful P3 result used an R128 target and a nominal R64 comparator. The GW R64 route was later found to retain a stale P2A geometry guard. A repair is queued; no GW comparator-based observability conclusion is final until that rerun completes. The R128 target outputs and candidate numerical-blocking outcomes are unaffected by this guard issue.
practical_implications: Do not claim practical speedup for the current Python S4/G8 research implementation on long daily workloads.
Do not treat G8 as robust across the tested daily panel because B02 and B05 fail numerically.
Do not tune dt or increase state count inside P3; any numerical-policy repair requires a separately frozen work unit.
